vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: apple-notes-applescript
Version: 1.1.0

The skill bundle contains a critical shell injection vulnerability in `scripts/notes-search.sh`. When the `--spotlight` flag is used, the user-provided `$QUERY` is directly interpolated into an `mdfind` command without proper sanitization, allowing for arbitrary command execution. While other scripts demonstrate good input sanitization for AppleScript, this specific flaw poses a significant risk. There is no evidence of intentional malicious behavior such as data exfiltration to external endpoints or persistence mechanisms.

llm.summary: This Apple Notes skill is purpose-related, but it needs review because it can modify/delete personal notes, silently export attachments, and contains input-handling bugs that could run unintended commands.

dimensions.detail: AppleScript access to Notes is expected for this skill, but direct access to the Notes group container and predictable exports under /tmp/notes-export are broader and less contained than basic Notes CRUD requires.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency fetch, remote payload retrieval, launch agent, or package mutation was found; the artifact consists of a skill markdown file and local shell scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose partial-match operations and a folder requirement for delete, but they do not clearly warn that read operations can copy attachments to disk, that delete acts on the first match without confirmation, or that some all-folder searches can touch a large sensitive corpus.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No root escalation or background persistence was found, but exported attachments are left as persistent local files in a predictable temporary directory, and delete/edit operations mutate Notes data without an in-script confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main purpose, Apple Notes listing/search/read/create/edit/delete, is coherent, but the package also includes attachment/PDF export behavior and direct reads from Apple Notes private storage that are not clearly surfaced in the main command table.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing. Use only with trusted note names, folder names, queries, and limits; keep operations scoped to specific folders; back up Notes before edit/delete; and avoid read/attachment/PDF export workflows until exports use a private directory and require explicit user approval.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: Broad access to personal notes is expected for an Apple Notes integration, but the reviewed artifacts under-disclose privacy impact, first-match destructive behavior, and read-time attachment export side effects.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The scripts directly inspect Apple Notes private group-container storage to locate attachment files, which is not clearly described by the skill's AppleScript-focused purpose or read command documentation.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Attachment extraction is a plausible add-on feature, but defaulting to /tmp/notes-export and allowing caller-selected output paths without permission checks or clear consent is unsafe for sensitive note contents.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The read script says it shows attachment information, but the implementation copies attachments to disk when attachment IDs are present, so the scanner concern is supported by artifact evidence.
[T09] unexpected: The static scan findings are supported: limit, folder, and Spotlight query values are interpolated into generated AppleScript without consistent validation or argument passing, creating command-execution risk from crafted inputs.
